title: Concept authoring result
description: Result contract for the concept-author agent, the named producer. The named consumer is the thin-path orchestrator (docs/bootstrap.md, step 3), which chooses its transition from the closed `state` field; until it exists, framework tests are the consumer. This artifact carries control flow, so it requires boundary validation before consumption per .claude/rules/contracts.md — that boundary check arrives with the orchestrator and is a named gap until then.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

producer.description: The agent this contract belongs to. A const, not a free string: a result claiming another producer is not an instance of this contract.

state.description: The closed set the consumer branches on: authored = a new concept file exists, updated = an existing one was revised, blocked = nothing was written and blocking_reason says why.

term.description: The term as delegated, so a result can be traced to its request without reading either.

concept_id.description: Id of the concept written, matching the id pattern of schemas/concept.v1.json.

concept_path.description: Repo-relative path of the concept file written.

files_changed.description: Every file the agent touched — the concept file and the index row at minimum. This is the evidence trail a reviewer diffs against.

blocking_reason.description: Why nothing was written: the missing input or the conflicting concept, named so the caller can act without re-running the agent to find out.
A blocking reason on a successful result is a contradiction; expressed as a dependency so the failure names the offending field.
